name: Healthcare PHI Baseline
description: Inline Web DLP detection of US healthcare PHI: MRN, patient account number, date of birth and legal sex as strong identifiers, anchored to clinical context by Zscaler's predefined medical dictionaries (Medical Information, Medical Document) plus a small custom clinical-phrase list. One presence engine (context + identifier, two distinct identifiers, or a legal-sex booster beside an identifier) and one bulk-export engine, bound to a single monitor-only rule with OCR on. Immutable: objects that drift from this definition are restored on the next deploy. Start in monitor (ALLOW), tune proximity and thresholds against real spreadsheets and multi-column PDFs, then move to BLOCK. Containment (File Type Control, Cloud App Control) is deliberately outside this pack.
references: Zscaler: About DLP Engines (All / Any / Sum operators, nesting limits)
notes: E_PHI_BULK_EXPORT is expressed as 'any identifier dictionary with 10 or more matches' rather than a Sum across dictionaries, because the engine expression language exposed through the API uses per-dictionary counts. If you want a true Sum, rebuild that engine in the portal's Engine Builder; the baseline will then report it as drifted, so remove it from dlp_engines.json first.

Proximity values are bytes across the extracted text stream. They are unreliable for spreadsheets, multi-column PDFs and OCR output; Branch B (two distinct identifiers) and the Medical Document ML dictionary cover those cases.
The rule sets no file_types, so it applies to every inspectable type; set file_types in dlp_policies.json to narrow it.
